title: Training module: counting the lost supply behind a replacement fill
content:
**Prescriptions & Renewals training — how much supply was lost.**

**The rule.** The lost supply is counted from the prescription's most recent dispensing, using the calendar days from that dispensing's date to the day of the replacement: where that is 14 days or fewer, the lost supply is the days until the next regular fill would have fallen due, that is, the early-refill share of the dispensing's days' supply rounded up to a whole day, less the days already elapsed; where it is 15 to 60 days, the lost supply is the days that dispensing would still have covered, that is, its days' supply less the days elapsed; where it is more than 60 days, the lost supply is one regular fill.

**Questions answered.**

*Which dispensing is used?* The most recent dispensing of this prescription on its fill ledger — its date and its days' supply.

*How are the days elapsed counted?* As the number of calendar days by which the day of the replacement falls after the dispensing date.

*What is "one regular fill"?* The per-fill days' supply recorded on the prescription.

*What does "rounded up" mean in the first band?* The early-refill share of the dispensing's days' supply is raised to the next whole day whenever it is not already whole, before the days elapsed are subtracted.

**The three bands.**

| Days since the most recent dispensing | Lost supply |
|---|---|
| 14 or fewer | early-refill share of that dispensing's days' supply, rounded up to a whole day, less the days elapsed |
| 15 to 60 | that dispensing's days' supply less the days elapsed |
| more than 60 | one regular fill: the per-fill days' supply recorded on the prescription |

**Worked cases (hypothetical; the early-refill shares below are example inputs only).**
- A 30-day dispensing 10 days ago, with an early-refill share of 80 percent: 24 days less 10 gives a lost supply of 14 days.
- A 30-day dispensing 6 days ago, with an early-refill share of 85 percent: 25.5 rounds up to 26, less 6 gives 20 days.
- A 30-day dispensing 14 days ago falls in the first band; 15 days ago it falls in the second: 30 less 15 gives 15 days.
- A 90-day dispensing 60 days ago: 90 less 60 gives 30 days. At 61 days the third band applies, and the lost supply is the per-fill days' supply on the prescription.
